**Revised Narrative:**

The enrichment analysis identified **Galactosemia (SMPDB SMP00182)** as the top-scoring pathway, with D-Glucose (C00221), Sucrose (C00089), Galactinol (C01235), myo-Inositol (C00137), Galactitol (C01697), and Glycerol (C00116) belonging to the broader **Galactose Metabolism (KEGG map00052 / SMPDB SMP00043)** network. The pathway-membership queries returned a co-occurrence plausibility of 1.0 for all six metabolites across these pathways. Within the galactose metabolic axis, D-Glucose feeds into downstream catabolism, Galactinol serves as a galactosyl donor, and Galactitol appears as a downstream polyol.

myo-Inositol (C00137) was confirmed in both **Galactose Metabolism** and **Phosphatidylinositol Phosphate Metabolism (KEGG map00562)**. Ethanolamine (C00189) and Glycerol (C00116) also belong to the confirmed metabolite set.

Dopamine (C03758), Squalene (C00751), and Inosine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate (C05768) were detected but do not appear in the top-enriched pathways returned by RaMP-DB.

**Limitations:** Claims involving Leloir pathway activation, osmolality/oxidative-stress consequences of galactitol accumulation, and neurotransmitter pathway annotation for dopamine could not be verified against the pathway databases and were omitted from this version. The narrative reflects only those compounds and pathways with confirmed membership in RaMP-DB.
